title: Nerikiri wagashi sculpting
summary: Nerikiri is a Japanese tea-room sweet made from tinted white-bean dough. The maker colours the dough in layers, wraps it around a smooth bean filling, then shapes a flower of the season with small bamboo and wooden tools.
howToPlay: Look at the framed picture: it shows the finished sweet, such as a camellia in winter or a chrysanthemum in autumn.
Choose a dough colour and tap each layer to tint it, then draw each flap of dough in over the filling.
Press the petal lines with the triangle stick, scrape the veins with the three-pronged scraper and sift the heart with the fine sieve.
Set the tiny stamens with the tweezers where the flower has them.
rules: Steps run in order; each is scored on its own and the scores are averaged.
A slow, steady press cuts a clean groove; a hurried one only scratches and counts for less.
A dough colour counts only on the layer it belongs to.
Your score reflects the colour and coverage of the layers and how closely your lines follow the guide.
heritageNote: Nerikiri is a seasonal confection of Japanese tea houses, made by hand from white bean paste softened with a little rice cake and tinted in a few colours. Each sweet takes the shape of a flower or leaf of the moment and is served alongside tea.
